title: Telco churn: a fixed 15-experiment campaign and deep tabular models
request: For a subscription business, find which modeling choices give a reliable churn-risk ranking, and whether deep tabular models beat simple ones on this kind of data.
spec: A fixed 15-experiment development campaign on the public Telco churn table with duplicate-grouped 2x3-fold CV, every preprocessing step fitted inside folds; a comparison of TabTransformer, FT-Transformer and SAINT against trees and logistic regression. Primary metrics ROC-AUC and average precision.
plan: Write the contract: one customer at the snapshot date, target Churn, customerID forbidden; note that the real prediction time and outcome window are not in the public data.
Fix the 15 experiments before running them: a prior-only floor, three logistic regressions, forests, boosting, and charge features for logistic regression and LightGBM.

Run them with exact duplicate input rows kept in one fold, imputation, encoding and derived features fitted per fold, and out-of-fold predictions, calibration, missing-input stress tests, data and code hashes saved.
Benchmark the deep tabular models against the same baselines.
Write CHURN_BENCHMARK.md as development evidence only.

decisions.decision: Keep exact duplicate input rows in the same fold.
decisions.why: A duplicate split across folds lets a model be scored on a row it has seen; the source has no household or account grouping to use instead.

decisions.decision: Label the leaderboard as development evidence.
decisions.why: The same CV is reused across all candidates and there is no independent test or event-time split.
It is an identifier; target-encoding it later inflated ROC-AUC from 0.82 to 1.00 in PIT-004.

change: dclab_rnd.churn_suite (run, status) writing results under research/churn-prediction/experiments/churn_exp/results with CHURN_BENCHMARK.md; tabular transformer scripts and a SAINT implementation under tabular_transformers/; first baselines and a teaching notebook under logistic_regression/.

measurements.name: 15-experiment churn campaign
measurements.gate: Rank fixed candidates by duplicate-grouped 2x3-fold development CV ROC-AUC, with AP and log loss beside it.
measurements.result: Logistic regression with charge features led: ROC-AUC 0.8499, AP 0.6708, log loss 0.4108; regularized histogram boosting 0.8478, regularized random forest 0.8472, regularized LightGBM 0.8468, plain logistic C=1 0.8448, Extra Trees baseline 0.8246, prior-only floor 0.5000. The top ten sit within 0.010.
measurements.next: Confirm the leader on a temporal or external split once the snapshot time and outcome window are known.

measurements.name: deep tabular models vs simple ones
measurements.gate: Same split and preprocessing for every model; compare ROC-AUC.
measurements.result: Logistic regression 0.845, FT-Transformer 0.842, XGBoost 0.842, SAINT 0.842, TabTransformer 0.833.
measurements.next: Do not spend on deep tabular models for this kind of table without a new reason.

outcome: A well-specified linear model matched or beat every boosted and transformer model on Telco churn (0.850 development CV). Independent confirmation is still pending because the public data lacks the prediction time.
lessons: On a small, clean, mostly categorical table, a logistic regression with sensible features is the bar the complex models must clear, and here none cleared it.
Differences of 0.002 to 0.005 between the top candidates are inside development-CV noise; the ranking is not a model choice.
